items.title: The manufacturing data gap holding back physical AI
items.summary: Robotics and physical AI companies have raised nearly $48 billion so far in 2026 , but the rollout of fully autonomous machines in industrial settings isn’t a given. For robots to step beyond controlled environments onto the manufacturing floor, they need real-world data to learn from. Most production facilities aren’t set up to provide it. Consider the welding process. For a robot to improve its technique autonomously, it needs to understand how changes in welding angle, travel speed, workpiece position, and other key parameters affect the finished result. Experienced technicians develop this understanding through years of hands-on experience, but much of that knowledge isn't captured in a form robotics partners can use to train autonomous systems. Sebastian Castro is an independent roboticist specializing in robotic manipulation. He is currently contracting with the Dexterous Robotics Group at NASA’s Johnson Space Center. Sebastian previously worked as a software engineer at the Robotics and AI (RAI) Institute, PickNik, Boston Dynamics, and the MIT Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence Laboratory (CSAIL), and in education marketing at MathWorks. He also devotes personal time to robotics education through blog posts, open-source software, mentorship, talks, and workshops.
